title: Ethiopian Roasted Chicken
author: Chef Haile
desc: Ethiopian Roasted Chicken — a whole chicken marinated overnight in berbere, kibbeh, garlic, and ginger, roasted until the berbere skin caramelises into a magnificently deep red crust. The showpiece roast — Ethiopia's berbere tradition applied to a whole chicken.
longDesc: Ethiopian roasted chicken applies the same berbere-kibbeh tradition to a whole roasted bird — the overnight marinade penetrates deeply, and the oven's dry heat caramelises the berbere on the skin into an extraordinary crust.
ingredients: 1 whole chicken (1.5 kg) — spatchcocked or whole
steps: Score chicken skin deeply. Push marinade under the skin and into every crevice.
Bring to room temperature 1 hour before roasting.
Baste with pan juices every 20 minutes.
The berbere skin should be deeply caramelised — dark red-brown and fragrant.
chefTips: Push marinade under the skin — it penetrates the meat rather than just colouring the exterior.
Spatchcocking (removing backbone) produces more even roasting.
The berbere crust should be dark but not burnt — watch carefully in the last 15 minutes.
commonMistakes: Not getting marinade under the skin.
cookingScience: The berbere marinade under the skin conducts heat more efficiently than a surface-only rub — the fat in the kibbeh acts as a heat conductor, creating a more even temperature distribution through the breast meat. The sugar content of the berbere caramelises under high heat, creating the characteristic dark crust.
sustainabilityTips: Whole chicken roasting — every part served.
healthBenefits: Less fat than fried chicken preparations.
culturalNote: Ethiopian roasted chicken is the restaurant showpiece — the whole bird arriving at the table, its berbere skin crackling and fragrant, announces that something serious has been prepared in the kitchen.
